explanation: Searched Mathlib for any declaration stating that `p (nth p ·)` is antitone (i.e. `a ≤ b → p (nth p b) → p (nth p a)`). Enumerated every `nth*` declaration in Mathlib (`grep` for `theorem/lemma nth…`), read Mathlib/Data/Nat/Nth.lean in full (all lemmas about `Nat.nth`: `nth_mem`, `nth_mem_of_lt_card`, `nth_mem_of_infinite`, `nth_le_nth'`, `le_nth`, `nth_eq_zero`, `nth_eq_zero_mono`, `nth_ne_zero_anti`, `count_nth`, `gc_count_nth`, …), and checked related files (`Data/Nat/Prime/Nth.lean`, `Order/OrderIsoNat.lean`, `SetTheory/Cardinal/Cofinality/Enum.lean`, `SetTheory/Ordinal/Enum.lean`). No other Mathlib declaration has this content: the existing lemmas either require the strict bound `n < #hf.toFinset` (`nth_mem`), only hold for infinite predicates, or are about `count`/monotonicity of the indices; none of them handles the `nth p a = 0` garbage-value case together with the hypothesis `p (nth p b)` the way this lemma does. The library's own proof uses only `nth_mem`, `nth_eq_zero` and case splitting, so there is no single Mathlib declaration it duplicates.
